definition: The name of 40 characters that Git calculates from the content of one file. One changed character gives another file hash. Git calls it a blob hash.
The change of a workflow pin. The service, one repository variable, and the workflow file of the consumer repository must change in a fixed order.
A commit in the service repository that changes a pinned value of the service configuration: a workflow pin or the package digest. Each one needs a deployment of the service.
One named value in an OIDC token, for example the repository or the commit. GitHub writes the claims and signs them. The job cannot change them.
The OIDC claim that names the workflow file in which the job is written: repository, path, and ref. For a job in a reusable workflow, it names the called file, not the caller.
A workflow file that another workflow calls with a "uses" line. It can be in another repository. The caller cannot change its steps.
The signed message of the Plan job that says that a commit needs no captures. The service then completes the Visonaut check as not required.
A named value in the settings of a GitHub repository. A workflow can read it. It is not in a file, so no pull request shows a change of it.
The repository of Visonaut itself: ariakit/visonaut. The service is deployed from its main branch.
